b1-outages.rule: Every internet-outage record maps to an ISO2 code through shared/country-code-resolve.ts; only GOVERNMENT_DIRECTED and MILITARY_ACTION outages active in the last 7 days score, and exam shutdowns (GOVERNMENT_DIRECTED records matched lexically on description and title, CII_OUTAGE_EXAM_TERMS, with negation bound to its own noun phrase) never do; overlapping records of one country count once, at the highest severity, and a record fades linearly to 0 over the last 24 hours of the window; a reader that maps 0 of N records reports unusable (P7b).
b1-outages.note: No fixture country moves: the committed fixtures were trimmed before cause and times were kept, so none of their outage records can score under the new rule, as none could before (0 of 15 mapped). Replaying the 2026-10-23T0946Z fixture with the untrimmed production outage records moves only RU, 62 to 63 (an ongoing MILITARY_ACTION partial outage since 2026-10-07).

b8-asn-outages.rule: An outage Radar files against networks (ASNs) and no country counts for the country Radar places the ASNs in only when its measured national impact (the ASNs' share of the country's NetFlows traffic in the week before x their traffic drop during the outage) exceeds CII_OUTAGE_ASN_NATIONAL_SHARE = 0.40; below it, or unmeasurable, it is excluded and reported (asnBelowNationalShare, asnImpactUnknown).
b8-asn-outages.note: No fixture carries asnOutages, so no fixture country moves. Over the year to 2026-10-23, no ASN outage cleared 40%: the four MILITARY_ACTION ones (DON-FTTH in RU three times, the VKontakte SPB data centre) measured 0.1% each and are excluded; the largest impact was 20.9% (Digicel Haiti, cause UNKNOWN). Live scores are unchanged. Sensitivity: any threshold from 0.30 to 0.50 gives the same verdicts on the year, because no ASN outage of any cause measured between 0.209 and 0.50.

b3-strike-precision.rule: One physical incident counts once, on the country hit, dated to its first report: the strike feed drops retrospective posts, interceptions and ships at sea, merges every report of one incident, and the scorer reads only the v2 strike tally (CII_STRIKE_TALLY_VERSION) that the fixed relay writes.
b3-strike-precision.note: No fixture country moves by 3 or more. The fixtures hold the relay's output, so the relay change cannot show in them. Rejecting their v1 tally moves IR 66 to 65 on 2026-10-23T0946Z and lowers blends by under 1 point elsewhere (IR, LB, SA, SY). A counterfactual on 2026-10-23T0946Z that swaps the production 72h window for the fixed relay's replay of the same posts moves SA 70 to 66 and IR 66 to 62 (PR #9592).

knownGaps.what: After deploy the scorer rejects the v1 tally and the relay starts a new v2 tally, so confirmed strike memory is the 72h window, not 21 days, until the v2 tally refills. GDELT's strike counter, merged by per-day max, keeps its own 21 days.
knownGaps.measured: On the committed fixtures (a v1 tally of 3 to 5 days, feed live since 2026-10-19): strike pressure P falls 19% for IR (18.6 to 15.2) and LB (24.3 to 19.6), 3% for SA (GDELT dominates), and SY 1.2 to 0; final scores move by at most 1.
knownGaps.modelled: For a steady campaign the 72h window holds 50% of the decayed 21-day pressure. The share held rises to 76% three days after deploy, 91% after a week and 99% after two weeks, and the gap closes at 21 days; the 30-day tally keeps days the scorer no longer weighs.
knownGaps.duration: up to 21 days after the relay deploy (the tally keeps 30 days, the scorer weighs 21)

knownGaps.what: Strict precision of counted strike events is below the I8 target of 80%, so the feed must not set a floor (Stage C).
knownGaps.measured: Production window 2026-10-20..23: 25% strict, 37% lenient (counting unexplained explosions). Same 311 posts through one model (gpt-oss-120b): base 31% / 43%, head 55-59% / 79-81%.
knownGaps.duration: until residual duplicates (one village under two spellings), undated claim footage and unexplained explosions are handled

With the full 365-day window the fixed writers fetch (dry run against the live UCDP API, 2026-10-23, events attributed where they happened), the 2026-10-23T0946Z fixture would read (family max): UA 94, SY 80, YE 79, IR 78, MM 69, LB 64, AF 63, IL 50 (advisory floor; UCDP term 19), PK 50 (advisory floor), MX 47, IN 38, BR 23.

attribution.rule: An event scores the place it happens (owner ruling, 2026-10-23). UCDP GED codes Gaza and West Bank events with country Israel (country_id 666) and names the territory in adm_1; the writers attribute rows whose adm_1 is Gaza Strip or West Bank to Palestine (ucdpLocatedCountry in scripts/shared/ucdp-candidate.cjs). Palestine (PS) is not one of the 31 scored countries, so these events feed no scored row. Israel uses Israel's own population (UN WPP 2024, 9.65M).

fixtures (legacy rows, no location), sum.note: before = Gaza counted to Israel over Israel plus Palestine population (15.34M); after = same rows over Israel's 9.65M. The fixtures cannot be re-attributed: their trimmed rows hold no adm_1 or coordinates.

b6-ucdp.conflictFamily: Conflict = min(100, max(acled + fatality + civilian, gdeltConflict, ucdp) + oref): UCDP deaths and GDELT CAMEO 18-20 coverage report the same war, so they merge by max, never by sum (P6). Independent review of 025dc0458. After B5 lands the form is min(100, max(acled + fatality + civilian, gdelt, ucdp) + oref). Moving from sum to max dropped YE (86 -> 80/79), SY (77/78 -> 74/75), AF (63/65 -> 61), IR (67/68 -> 65/67) and IL (55/53/56 -> 51/50/53) below the 3-point bar against v14; Conflict falls wherever UCDP and GDELT both fired.

b7-palestine.rule: An event scores the place where it happens (owner ruling, 2026-10-23): Gaza and West Bank events count for Palestine (PS), not Israel (IL). PS is not one of the 31 scored countries, so they score no row. v14 folded PS into IL in four places, all removed here: the border file merged the PS polygon into Israel's (ATTRIBUTED_TERRITORIES in scripts/generate-cii-country-borders.mjs), so every coordinate input did; ciiCountryForIso2 mapped a PS-coded strike event and the strike tally's PS days to IL; COUNTRY_KEYWORDS.IL held 'gaza'; and the strike feed's gazetteer filed GeoNames' 'Judea and Samaria Area' (the West Bank) under IL. A strike event without a country code whose coordinates are on land is now placed by them, never by its text, as earthquakes already were: the text names the attacker as often as the place.
